app.name: Readi
app.tagline: Practise tech interviews with an AI interviewer and get honest, specific feedback.

landing.heading: Honest feedback before the interview that counts.
landing.lead: Practise with an AI interviewer that asks follow-up questions. Then read feedback that quotes your own answers and shows you what to fix.
landing.inTheOpen: Readi is being built in the open. Today you can set up your profile and CV; mock interviews, feedback reports and study plans are on the way.
landing.freeNote: Free plan: 3 text mock interviews every month. Frontend, backend, QA and full-stack.

example.caption: Example feedback from a frontend mock interview
example.question: Interviewer: a product page is slow on older Android phones. What would you do?
example.answerQuote1: open the React Profiler and see which components re-render
example.answerQuote2: use useMemo everywhere so the page is faster
example.answerAfter: , and lazy-load the images below the fold.”
example.notesLabel: The mentor’s notes on this answer
example.note1: Good start: you measured before you changed anything.
example.note2: Memoisation has a cost. Say when it helps, and how you’d check that it did.
example.evidence: Every score comes with the words it is based on.

problem.heading: The feedback you never get
problem.p1: A rejection email tells you the decision, not the reason. The interviewer won’t tell you either. So the same gaps travel with you to the next interview, and the one after that.
problem.p2: Reading about interviews is not the same as answering out loud, with someone asking “why?” after every answer.
problem.p3: Readi is the interviewer who does tell you: specifically, kindly, and before it matters.
problem.note: Every mark Readi gives you comes with a quote from your own answer, so you can see what it is based on.

session.heading: What a practice session looks like
session.step1Body: Your role and level, the kind of interview, and 15, 30 or 45 minutes. By text, or by voice if your connection allows.
session.step2Body: The interviewer asks up to two follow-up questions on each answer, aimed at what you left out.
session.step3Body: Your strengths, the three things to fix first, and what a strong answer covers — with a lesson for each gap.

audience.heading: Who it’s for
audience.body: Frontend, backend, QA and full-stack engineers, from intern to mid-level. If you are getting ready for your first technical interview, or aiming for a remote role abroad, the questions meet you where you are.

cost.heading: What it costs
cost.body: Start free, with 3 text mock interviews every month. Paid plans are priced in naira, weekly or monthly, and you can cancel in one click. Outside Nigeria, pay in US dollars.
cost.note: Built for your phone and your data: text interviews are light on bandwidth, and voice falls back to text if your signal drops.

closing.heading: Hear the hard questions here first.
closing.body: Your first session is a 15-minute diagnostic interview. It shows where you stand today and builds your study plan.

v1.title: Process my voice during interviews
v1.body: Your speech is converted to text by our speech-recognition provider so the AI interviewer can respond and give feedback.

v1.title: Keep recordings of my interviews
v1.body: Recordings are stored for 30 days so you can listen back, then deleted automatically.

v1.title: Camera coaching

diagnostic.title: Start with a diagnostic interview
diagnostic.body: A 15-minute mixed interview that shows where you stand today. Four questions, typed, with follow-ups — the way a first round actually goes.
diagnostic.note: You can end it early, and nothing about it is shared with anyone.
diagnostic.taken: Take another interview whenever you like — the questions you have already been asked are put aside first.

list.title: Practice
list.lead: Your mock interviews, and the next one whenever you are ready.
list.empty: You have not taken a mock interview yet. The first one takes fifteen minutes and tells you where you stand.
list.active: You have an interview in progress. Starting a new one leaves that one unfinished.
list.scope: Every interview here is a conversation you type: questions, follow-ups, and the chance to ask your own at the end. Coding and whiteboard rounds are not part of it yet.

setup.title: Set up your interview
setup.lead: Choose how long you have and what you want to be asked about. You can end it early at any point.
setup.lengthHint: The clock runs from the interviewer's first word to the end, whatever happens in between.
setup.role: Which role are you interviewing for?
setup.levelNone: This role has no levels on offer yet.
setup.stackHint: Stack-specific questions only exist for a variant we offer. Anything else gets the general questions for the role — a real interview, just not about your framework.
setup.tellUsHint: This does not change the questions you are asked. We read it when deciding which variants to build next, and it is saved to your profile.
setup.types: What should the interviewer ask about?
setup.typesHint: All of them is the mixed interview a first round usually is. Narrow it when you want to drill one thing.
setup.typesRequired: Pick at least one kind of question.
setup.scope: How you explain your work, your judgement, and how you hold up when a question is pushed further. It is not a coding round and not a whiteboard — those are not built yet, and we would rather say so than imply otherwise.
setup.noRoles: There are no roles on offer yet.

complete.title: Interview finished
complete.lead: You answered {asked} of {budget} questions in {minutes} minutes.
complete.leadUnfinished: This one was left unfinished after {asked} of {budget} questions.
complete.waiting: Saving the last of the transcript.
complete.scoring: The whole conversation is recorded. Rubric-based feedback and your readiness score arrive in the next update, and this session is scored then — none of what you just did is thrown away.
complete.next: Read the interview back and mark the answers you would rather give again. Then take another one: the questions you have already been asked are put aside first.
complete.noTurns: Nothing was said in this one.

sections.rolesLead: The roles a candidate prepares for, and what each one offers.
sections.levelsLead: The ladder a role is hired at, lowest first.
sections.stacksLead: The variants a role is interviewed for, like Java / Spring.

content.workflow: A content expert writes and submits; an admin publishes. Candidates only ever see published content — and a lesson also needs its track published, a question its rubric.

markdown.hint: Markdown. Headings, lists, links and code.

question.slugHint: Permanent: the seed files and the importer match on it. Lowercase words joined by hyphens.
question.rolesHint: A question may suit more than one role.
question.stacksHint: Leave every box clear unless the question is specific to those stacks — tagging narrows who is ever asked it. An untagged question goes to everyone preparing for its roles.
question.subtopicHint: Optional, freer than the topic: 'useEffect', 'index design'.
question.difficultyHint: 1 is a warm-up, 5 is hard for the level it is aimed at.
question.promptHint: What the interviewer asks, in the interviewer's words.
question.contextHint: Optional: what the candidate is given before the question.
question.rubricHint: Only a published rubric lets a question be published.
question.idealPointsHint: The answer key. Never shown to a candidate; the evaluator scores against it.
question.followUpsHint: Answer key. The opening question asks one thing; each remaining criterion gets the probe the interviewer may ask if the answer has not already covered it.
question.followUpProbePlaceholder: How would you know your list was enough?
question.followUpsNeedRubric: Choose a rubric first — a follow-up names the criterion it probes.
question.followUpsOverCap: A criterion may have at most {max} follow-ups. Needing a third means it scores too many things to be one criterion.

rubric.name: Name
rubric.criteriaHint: Between 2 and 8. The weights must add up to 100.
rubric.levelsHint: 0 is absent, 4 is excellent. Two readers of the same answer should land on the same number.

track.title: Title
track.roleLevelHint: Only one track may be published per role and level.
track.topicsHint: Core topics drive the readiness score.
track.modulesHint: A module has no status of its own: it is published with its track.
track.noModules: No modules yet. A track needs at least one before it can be published.
track.noLessons: No lessons in this module yet.

topic.name: Name
topic.descriptionHint: One line, for the people writing content.

review.badgeHint: A model drafted this and nobody has marked it reviewed. It can be published here for development, but in production publishing it is refused until someone has.
review.lead: A model drafted this. Mark it reviewed once you have read it and stand behind it — the question, its answer key and every level descriptor of its rubric.
review.confirm: Mark this reviewed? It records your name against it, and it is what lets it be published in production.
